clue.text: As quick as a parasitologist is keeping wicket?

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a scientist who studies parasites might be said to be keen on, or into, ticks
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about how fast a parasite scientist would be if asked to keep wicket at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts W inside INTO TICKS, splitting INTO into IN TWO. The definition completes the phrase 'as quick as …'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very soon or very fast, so it finishes the comparison begun by these words.

clue.text: Child's cooler if wearing fashionable hat

definitions.note: an adjective meaning belonging to or typical of a child, standing in for the possessive

indicators.note: the cooler is dressed in the other pieces, so it sits within them

parts.note: in means fashionable
tile is old slang for a hat
a fan cools you

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a child would be cooler wearing a trendy hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantile describes things of babyhood and early youth, as a child's ways are.

clue.text: Loathsome, as far as a pretty girl is concerned

parts.note: to, as in 'up to' or 'as far as' a point
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: Someone explains what they find repulsive where a beautiful woman is concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: TOADISH means like a toad, a byword for repulsiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a toad, a creature traditionally thought ugly and repellent, hence disgusting.

clue.text: Simplify a couple of clues before complaint finally begins

indicators.note: begins says that letter goes at the front
finally picks the final letter of the word complaint

parts.note: this clue is 3-down, and the clue two places earlier is labelled 1-down

explanation.surface: Advice to make things simpler by easing up on clues before a grumble starts.
explanation.walkthrough: A self-referential clue: the light two before 3-down is One Down. 'complaint finally' gives T, which 'begins' puts in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate or soften something, such as language, making it less extreme or demanding.

clue.text: Go over promise with one of my best friends and me?

definitions.note: the setter speaking of themself, a noun phrase

parts.note: to cross is to go over
giving your word is promising
a setter is a breed of dog, man's best friend

explanation.surface: The speaker describes going over a promise with a close friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of the puzzle is the 'me'; a dog is proverbially man's best friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who compiles the puzzle is the one speaking through this clue.

clue.text: This is at odds with my place of work

indicators.note: at odds suggests things out of their usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that this situation conflicts with their workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A forge where a blacksmith toils is a workshop, a place of labour.

clue.text: Catch end of baby's crib

parts.note: to cop is to catch

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word baby

explanation.surface: A command to grab the end of the infant's cot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crib' looks like a cot, but here it means to copy someone's work.
explanation.definitionFit: To crib is to plagiarise or reproduce another's work, a synonym.

clue.text: Time of depression, maybe, in eastern UK town

indicators.note: of says the time belongs to the depression, so it follows

parts.note: a col is a dip between mountain peaks, one kind of depression
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: The Depression era, perhaps, in a town in the east of the UK.
explanation.walkthrough: COLERAINE is a town in Northern Ireland, so not eastern at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleraine is a town in County Londonderry, Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Under pressure, abandon vital game

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece comes after the upper, so this goes beneath

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
to lay off is to stop or give up

explanation.surface: A team is told to abandon a crucial match while under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciding extra match that settles a tie is crucial to the outcome.

clue.text: Wretched old bird

parts.note: flaming is a mild British curse word, like 'wretched' or 'blasted'

explanation.surface: Someone curses an aged feathered creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink wading bird with long legs, a specific example.

clue.text: Most definitely not good for one

parts.note: ill means bad, not good
say means for example, as in 'one instance'

explanation.surface: A firm declaration that something is not good for an individual.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic exclamation of agreement, meaning absolutely or certainly.

clue.text: Secure network protecting one's back

indicators.note: back says the whole is read in reverse
protecting means guarding something within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: LAN is a local area network
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Advice to fasten a network that guards someone's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts I in LAN to make LIAN, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten something firmly in place, as with a hammered pin.

clue.text: Recording by school that's ground-breaking

parts.note: a disc is a record
Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: An innovative record released by a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground-breaking' suggests pioneering; literally the tool breaks up soil. HARROW is a famous fee-paying school near London.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm implement with sharp discs that cuts up the soil, literally breaking the ground.

clue.text: Lives next to club owned by female author

indicators.note: owned by the woman puts her before the club, as in her possession

parts.note: is, as in exists or lives
her refers to a woman
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Someone lives next to a club run by a woman writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was an English novelist, writer of Goodbye to Berlin.

clue.text: Like pie? With vegetables and last of gravy, especially so!

definitions.note: extremely simple, an adjectival phrase intensifying the preceding idea

parts.note: the saying goes 'easy as pie'
peas are vegetables

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of gravy

explanation.surface: A pie served with vegetables and gravy, all the more so.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on what comes before: like pie, especially so, means very simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish rhyming phrase meaning extremely simple, even more effortless than ordinary.

clue.text: Instant judgment initially dubious

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of judgment

parts.note: iffy means doubtful or dubious

explanation.surface: A snap verdict that starts off doubtful.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun meaning a moment, as in 'back in a moment'.

clue.text: My tribute to thrash metal

indicators.note: to thrash something is to beat it about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A band dedicates a song to thrash metal music.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrash metal is a heavy rock genre; here 'thrash' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare-earth element, a silvery metallic chemical element named after Ytterby in Sweden.

clue.text: Turn up with possible substitute for stick: carrot?

parts.note: to root is to dig up, as pigs do
a riding crop can replace a stick, as in 'carrot and stick'

explanation.surface: Carrot and stick: an alternative to the stick turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: The carrot-and-stick saying misleads; the carrot is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is one example of a vegetable grown for its edible underground part.

clue.text: First of editors on the Times to make history?

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after

parts.note: eras are times or periods

indicators.note: First of picks the first letter of editors

explanation.surface: The chief editor of The Times newspaper making history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Times' looks like the newspaper but means ERAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out something, so that it is gone and past, is to make it history.

clue.text: Explorer mostly just consuming beer

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the beer goes inside
mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: right means just or fair
ale is beer

explanation.surface: An adventurer simply drinking beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like an adverb meaning simply, but it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was an Elizabethan adventurer and voyager to the Americas.

clue.text: Person who's left dangerous dose finished unconscious

parts.note: OD is an overdose
done means finished
out means knocked out, unconscious

explanation.surface: Someone takes a perilous overdose and is found unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider, the one excluded or remaining apart from a group.

clue.text: Outside broadcast following sporting event

indicators.note: following says this piece comes after the other

parts.note: an open is a tournament, such as golf's Open
to air is to broadcast

explanation.surface: A TV outside broadcast after a sports fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Held outdoors, rather than within a building.

clue.text: Some fungus spreads across touching edges

indicators.note: the fungus extends across the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: ceps are a kind of mushroom
re means about or touching on

explanation.surface: Some fungus grows across, its margins touching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreads' looks like the definition, but it is part of the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge is to move slowly and stealthily, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Rep left cup game, tense

indicators.note: game here means lame or crippled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sales representative left a cup match, feeling nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like a nervous state; it is the grammatical term. Game, as in a gammy leg, is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A past-perfect verb form, formed with 'had', is a grammatical tense.

clue.text: Some backing free vote for change of course

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some MPs backing a free vote on changing policy direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve or alter direction, a verb for changing course.

clue.text: Worried by difficulty, become obsessed

indicators.note: by means next to, placing the pieces side by side

parts.note: a fix is a difficult situation
ate, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: Fretting over a problem until it becomes an obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: To fixate is to dwell compulsively on something.

clue.text: Dish of rabbit I had on the train regularly

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after
regularly picks every other letter of the words the train

parts.note: rabbit is British slang for chatter, as is yak

explanation.surface: A rabbit dish eaten on the train.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for to talk endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese dish of meat or fish glazed in a soy sauce marinade.

clue.text: Watery part of course abandoned by arachnophobe

definitions.text: Watery part of course abandoned by arachnophobe

parts.words: Watery part of course abandoned by arachnophobe
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme, Little Miss Muffet ate curds and a thin liquid, then fled from a spider

explanation.surface: A spider-fearer leaves the thin part of a meal behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Miss Muffet, eating curds and whey, was frightened away by a spider.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin liquid left after milk curdles, part of the curds-and-whey meal.

clue.text: Barer of glad tidings (using central Post Office)?

definitions.text: Barer of glad tidings (using central Post Office)?

parts.words: Barer of glad tidings (using central Post Office)?
parts.note: a messenger who undresses to deliver the message; the bracket notes the PO in the middle of the spelling

explanation.surface: A messenger with good news, sent via the main post office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barer' puns on bearer; the bracket tells you the central letters are PO, not the PPER of an alternative spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip-tease performer sent to deliver a greeting, who bares all.
